name: Zaccur
overview: Zaccur was a male Levite distinguished as the son of Asaph and was set apart to prophesy through music using lyres, harps, and cymbals. He held a significant role among the musicians of Israel, being chosen third by lot among the singers, reflecting his important position in the worship ministry of the temple.
namesAndTitles: The name Zaccur means 'remembering,' a proper name given not directly by God but recorded in Scripture. This name highlights a theme of remembrance, though the biblical text does not elaborate further on its significance.
familyAndRelationships: Zaccur is explicitly identified as the son of Asaph, a notable figure associated with temple music. Additionally, it is inferred that Micaiah was his father, providing some genealogical context within the tribe of Levi. Beyond these, Scripture does not record further family relationships for Zaccur.
scriptureSignificance: Zaccur's importance lies in his role within the Levitical musicians who were divinely appointed to prophesy and lead worship through instrumental music. Being chosen third by lot among the singers underscores his recognized leadership and service in the temple's musical ministry. His association with Asaph connects him to a prominent lineage of worship leaders who contributed to Israel's spiritual life.
